quests.instruction: In “knee”, the k is silent. Which word starts with a silent k?
quests.hint: Say each word and notice which one starts with /n/.
quests.explanation: “Knit” starts with /n/. The k stays silent. In “kit” and “kid”, the k says /k/.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people pronounced the k in words like knee and knight. Today we only see it in the spelling.

quests.instruction: In “write”, the w is silent. Which word begins with a silent w?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the first sound. Which one starts with /r/?
quests.explanation: “Wrap” starts with /r/, and the w is silent. “Wag” and “wasp” both start with /w/.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with a silent g?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which one starts with the /n/ sound?
quests.explanation: “Gnat” starts with /n/, and the g is silent. “Gap” starts with /g/ and “gem” starts with /j/.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? __ee — it bends in the middle of your leg.
quests.hint: Say the word. The first sound is /n/, but think about the spelling.
quests.explanation: “Knee” starts with the letters kn. The k is silent and the ee spells long e.
quests.funFact: Knee, knit, knot, know and knife all begin with a silent k.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? __ite — you do this when you put words on paper.
quests.hint: The word starts with /r/. Which two letters spell it here?
quests.explanation: “Write” starts with wr. The w is silent and the i_e makes long i.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with the same sound as “nap”?
quests.hint: Say nap and say each word. Which one starts with /n/?
quests.explanation: “Nap” and “knot” both start with /n/. In “knot”, the k is silent.

quests.instruction: In “lamb”, the b is silent. Which word ends with a silent b?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen for /b/ at the end.
quests.explanation: “Thumb” ends with /m/ and the b is silent. “Tub” and “tab” end with /b/.
quests.funFact: Thumb, lamb, comb and climb all end with a silent b.

quests.instruction: Which word has a silent b after the letter m?
quests.hint: Look for the letters mb together.
quests.explanation: “Climb” has mb at the end, and the b is silent. “Clam” and “clamp” have no silent letters.

quests.instruction: “Comb” has a silent letter. How many sounds can you actually hear?
quests.hint: Count only the sounds you can hear. Silent letters do not count.
quests.explanation: “Comb” has 3 sounds: /k/ /ō/ /m/. The b is silent.

quests.instruction: After a short vowel, /ch/ is often spelled tch. Which word ends with tch?
quests.hint: Look for the three letters tch at the end.
quests.explanation: “Catch” ends with tch after a short vowel. “Coach” has a long vowel and ends with ch.
quests.funFact: Catch, match, patch, pitch and kitchen all use tch after a short vowel.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? ma__ — you light one to make fire.
quests.hint: The vowel is short, so think of the longer spelling.
quests.explanation: “Match” ends with tch after short a. The t is silent in sound but helps show the vowel is short.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with ch, not tch?
quests.hint: Look at the letter before the ch. Is it a vowel or a consonant?
quests.explanation: “Lunch” ends with ch because a consonant, n, comes before it. “Patch” and “pitch” have tch after short vowels.

quests.instruction: At the end of a short word, y can say long i. Which word has that sound?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which one ends with the long i sound?
quests.explanation: “My” ends with y, which says long i. “Me” has long e and “may” has long a.

quests.instruction: At the end of a longer word, y often says long e. Which word ends with that sound?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the very last sound.
quests.explanation: “Happy” ends with y saying long e. “Hand” ends with /d/ and “hippo” ends with long o.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT end with the long e sound spelled y?
quests.hint: Listen to the very end of each word. One does not finish with a long e sound.
quests.explanation: “Baby” and “candy” end with long e. “Sky” is a short word, so y says long i.
quests.funFact: The letter y can act like a vowel. In “gym” it even says short i.

quests.instruction: The letters ie can say long i, like in “pie”. Which word has that sound?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which one has the long i sound?
quests.explanation: “Tie” has ie saying long i. “Tip” has short i and “tea” has long e.
quests.funFact: Pie, tie and lie all use ie for the long i sound.

quests.instruction: The letters ea can say short e. Which word has short e spelled ea?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the vowel. Which one is short?
quests.explanation: “Bread” has ea saying short e. “Bean” and “beach” have long e.

quests.instruction: Which word spells long e with the letters ey?
quests.hint: Look at the ending of each word.
quests.explanation: “Key” ends with ey saying long e. “Kit” has short i and “kite” has long i.

quests.instruction: In some words, i says long i before nd or ld. Which word has long i?
quests.hint: Say each word out loud. Which one makes the i sound like the letter’s name?
quests.explanation: “Find” has long i. The nd ending changes the vowel. “Fin” and “fist” have short i.
quests.funFact: Find, kind, mind, wild and child all have a long vowel before nd or ld.

quests.instruction: Which word has the long o sound before ld?
quests.hint: Look for the word that ends with ld.
quests.explanation: “Cold” has long o before ld. “Cod” and “cot” have short o.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same vowel sound as “child”?
quests.hint: Say child and listen to the vowel. Match it.
quests.explanation: “Child” and “wild” both have long i. “Will” has short i and “wall” has /aw/.

quests.instruction: After w, the letter a often says /o/. Which word has that sound?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which vowel sound is different from the usual a?
quests.explanation: In “wash”, the a follows w and says /o/. “Wag” has short a and “wave” has long a.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /o/ sound spelled a?
quests.hint: The vowel comes right after sw. Say each word.
quests.explanation: “Swan” has a saying /o/ after w. “Swam” has short a.

quests.instruction: Which word has a different a sound from the other two?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the a.
quests.explanation: “Wag” and “wax” have short a. “Want” has a saying /o/.
quests.funFact: The letter w can change the sound of the vowel that follows it, as in water and was.

quests.instruction: The letters qu make the sounds /k/ and /w/ together. Which word starts with qu?
quests.hint: Say the first sounds of each word.
quests.explanation: “Queen” starts with /k/ + /w/ spelled qu. In English words the letter q is almost always followed by u.
quests.funFact: The letter q is almost always followed by u in English words.

quests.instruction: Tap out “quick” on your fingers. How many sounds is it?
quests.hint: Remember that qu makes two sounds and ck makes one.
quests.explanation: “Quick” has 4 sounds: /k/ /w/ /i/ /k/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the /ks/ sound spelled x?
quests.hint: Say each word slowly. Do you hear two sounds at the end of one of them?
quests.explanation: “Fox” ends with /k/ + /s/, spelled x. “Fog” ends with /g/ and “fork” ends with /k/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a silent letter at the start?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen for the first sound.
quests.explanation: “Write” starts with /r/ and the w is silent. “Wide” and “win” start with /w/.
quests.funFact: Write, wrap, wrist and wrong all begin with a silent w.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with tch?
quests.hint: Look at how each word finishes. One has three letters at the end that spell /ch/.
quests.explanation: “Pitch” ends with tch. “Pinch” ends with nch and “pick” ends with ck.

quests.instruction: In which word does y say long i?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the vowel at the end.
quests.explanation: “Try” ends with y saying long i. “Tray” has long a and “trim” has short i.
